title: Scheduling, Coordination, Admission and Backpressure
results: Eligibility, Admission, Queueing, Scheduling and Dispatch are distinct.
Admission commits ownership/identity/capacity obligations while dispatch later crosses the physical provider boundary.
A queue is a stateful waiting-work ownership contract, not merely work that is not running yet.
Current Runtime has no capacity-waiting queue; full capacity rejects work before Job/Attempt/reservation creation.
CONCURRENCY_LIMIT is explicit pre-commit admission refusal/backpressure with scoped capacity/holder evidence rather than a queue receipt.
retryAfterMs is a retry hint rather than reservation, priority guarantee or scheduled wakeup.
Upper-layer retry/re-admission is distinct from Runtime queueing.
Runtime Release provides specialized admitted dispatch deferral: an Accepted reserved Job can be dispatched later by reconciliation without constituting a capacity queue.
Ordinary newly admitted Jobs reserve capacity then immediately attempt dispatch after the lifecycle critical section.
Scheduling selects among eligible owned contenders; admission and dispatch remain separate mechanisms.
One-active-execution-per-Workspace is a coordination/serialization invariant rather than hardware scheduling policy.
FIFO, priority, fairness and deadline orderings are explicit policies rather than neutral mechanics.
SJF/SRT-like policies require workload-duration prediction that generic Runtime does not possess as truth.
Priority can starve and aging/fairness introduce explicit equity/value objectives.
Linux CFS/EEVDF demonstrates scheduler fairness and latency are explicit objectives backed by dedicated accounting state.
Deadline scheduling requires execution-demand/feasibility assumptions and cannot create capacity.
Unbounded queues turn persistent overload into growing latency/storage/staleness; bounded queues merely move the overload boundary.
Backpressure can be refusal/credit/blocking and does not require queueing; flow control and congestion control are scoped distinct mechanisms.
Capacity rejection is not value-aware load shedding and generic Runtime lacks a cross-domain value owner.
A Runtime-owned queue would require durable waiting-item identity, persistence, cancellation, expiry, policy/environment revalidation, fairness and recovery semantics.
Current queue-less refusal keeps future-work strategy with Host/Agent/domain owners rather than silently creating Runtime obligations.
Queue/scheduler introduction remains unjustified until concrete repeated workloads falsify explicit refusal plus upper-layer strategy and supply a stable scheduling objective.

nextRound.title: Failure, Recovery, Retry, Idempotency and Exactly-Once
nextRound.entryQuestion: When execution or communication fails or becomes ambiguous, what may safely be repeated, recovered, resumed, reconciled or compensated, and at which boundary can any exactly-once claim actually hold?

notes: RF9 explains current queue-less admission/backpressure and specialized dispatch deferral but does not authorize queue, scheduler, priority/fairness, load shedding, preemption or retry changes.
